Need a passport size photo today? Our passport size photo maker turns any picture into a correctly sized, print-ready image in under two minutes. Choose your country and document, upload a photo, and let the tool do the rest. It crops your image to the right dimensions, replaces the background and checks the result against official rules.

Whether you need a 35×45 mm photo for a UK or Schengen application, a 2×2 inch photo for a US visa, or a custom size for another country, you can create a passport picture online right on this page. No studio visit, no ruler and no photo editing skills required.

How to Make a Passport Size Photo Online in 3 Steps

Follow these three steps to make a passport picture online. The whole process takes about two minutes.

Upload Your Photo

Select your country and document type first, such as passport, visa, ID card or driving licence. The tool then loads the official size, resolution and background rules. Next, take a new photo with your phone or pick one from your gallery.

  • Face the camera directly and keep your head level.
  • Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed.
  • Stand facing a window for soft, even light.
  • Ask a friend to shoot from about 1.5 metres (5 feet) away to avoid distortion.

Any background works, because the tool replaces it for you.

Auto-Crop & Background Fix

Once you upload your image, the tool finds your face, removes the old background and applies the colour your document requires. It then crops the frame to the exact passport size.

Feature: Instant passport size crop

Manual cropping is where most people go wrong. Our tool uses facial landmark detection to place your eyes, chin and crown within the ratios that government guidelines demand. You get the right head size and the right margins without any guesswork.

Download, Print or Share

Preview your result, then download it. Use the digital file for online applications, such as the US DS-160 visa form or the UK passport renewal portal. Choose the print option when a paper application needs physical photos.

Feature: Ready-to-print copies on one sheet

The print template places several correctly sized photos on a single 4×6 inch sheet. Take it to any local photo printer or print shop and cut the photos apart. Ask for real photo paper, because plain office paper often gets rejected.

Why Use Our Passport Size Photo Maker?

Wrong sizing is the most common reason passport and visa photos get rejected. The head is too small, the crop is off-centre or the resolution is too low. Our passport picture maker solves these problems at the source.

  • Country-specific profiles: Every supported country has its own stored width, height, head-to-frame ratio, resolution and background colour.
  • AI background removal: The tool separates you from any background and swaps in the required white, off-white, light grey or light blue.
  • Biometric cropping: Face detection positions your head to match official percentages, not just a rough guess.
  • Automatic quality checks: Before you download, the tool checks sharpness, lighting, eye visibility, head tilt and output resolution.
  • Digital and print output: Get a standalone file for online forms and a print sheet for paper applications.

Passport Size Photo Specifications

There is no single universal passport size. Each country sets its own dimensions, head height and background colour. This table shows the formats people request most often. Select your country in the tool above and it applies the right specification for you.

Country or document Photo size Head height Background
United States (passport and visa)2×2 in (51×51 mm)1 to 1⅜ inWhite
United Kingdom (passport)35×45 mm29–34 mmLight grey or cream
Schengen visa (Europe)35×45 mm32–36 mmPlain light grey or white
India (passport and visa)51×51 mm, or 35×45 mm on some formsVaries by formWhite
Canada (passport)50×70 mm31–36 mmWhite

Rules change, so always check your embassy or passport authority for the latest requirements before you apply. Two of the most common formats are the 35×45 mm standard used across the UK, Europe and many other countries, and the 2×2 inch format used for US documents. Our tool supports both, plus many more.

Background Requirement: White background, face centred and evenly lit

A clean background and good lighting decide whether a photo passes. Most countries ask for a plain white background, but some use light grey, cream or light blue. The UK, for example, requires light grey or cream, not white. Our tool applies the correct colour for your document automatically.

Whatever the country, aim for these basics:

  • Centred face: Your head sits in the middle of the frame, with your shoulders visible.
  • Even lighting: No shadows on your face or behind you, and no glare on your skin.
  • Neutral expression: Eyes open, mouth closed, no smiling or raised eyebrows.
  • Clear view of your face: Hair away from your eyes, no sunglasses and no hat. Check your country's rule on glasses, because some countries ban them entirely.
  • Sharp image: No blur, no filters and no heavy retouching.

Common reasons passport photos get rejected:

  • The wrong size or head height for the country.
  • The wrong background colour, or shadows behind you.
  • Glare, blur or low resolution.
  • A tilted head, a smile or closed eyes.
  • An old photo that no longer looks like you.
  • Filters, beauty modes or heavy retouching.

Our automatic checks flag most of these problems before you download, so you can retake the photo instead of losing days to a rejected application.

Students, travellers, professionals and families all use the tool. It works for emergency renewals when speed matters and for planned applications when you want to avoid studio prices. HR teams also use it to prepare employee immigration documents.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the standard passport size photo?

No single size applies everywhere. The two most common formats are 35×45 mm, used in the UK, Schengen countries and many others, and 2×2 inches (51×51 mm), used for US passports and visas. Canada uses 50×70 mm. Our tool stores the correct size for each supported country and applies it automatically.

Can I make a passport size photo from my phone gallery?

Yes. Pick any clear photo from your gallery and upload it. Choose one where your face looks straight at the camera, your expression is neutral and the light is even. Modern phone cameras give more than enough resolution. If your gallery has no suitable picture, take a new one facing a window and upload that instead.

Is the passport size photo maker free to use?

Uploading, processing and previewing your photo is free, so you can see the result before you pay. You pay only if you choose to download the full-resolution, watermark-free file or print template. There are no subscriptions or hidden charges.

Will my photo meet government requirements?

We build the tool against the official specifications published by each country's passport authority or embassy. If your original photo shows your face clearly and follows the basic guidelines above, the output should meet size and quality requirements. Always confirm current rules with the issuing authority.

What if my background is not white or plain?

That is fine. The background removal works on coloured, busy and patterned backgrounds. It extracts your face and replaces the background with the correct colour for your document.

Can I use this for visas, ID cards and other documents?

Yes. The tool covers passports, visas, national ID cards, driving licences and residence permits. Each document type has its own stored profile, so you always get the right dimensions.

What resolution does a passport photo need?

It depends on the authority. UK online uploads need at least 600×750 pixels. US digital photos must be square, between 600×600 and 1200×1200 pixels. Print photos need a high resolution of about 300 to 600 DPI. Our tool outputs the right pixel size for the document you select.

Ready to start? Use the tool above to create your passport size photo now, then download, print or share it in minutes.

title: UK Passport Photo Requirements – Size & Free Online Checker

h1: UK Passport Photo Requirements — Free Online Checker, Crop & Size Tool
content:
Meet Every British Passport Photo Requirement — Instantly Online

Getting your UK passport photo wrong is one of the most common reasons passport applications are delayed or rejected. Our free tool checks your photo against all official British passport photo specifications — dimensions, background colour, head size, lighting, and expression — and corrects any issues automatically. Upload your existing photo or take a new one, select UK Passport, and download a print-ready or digital file that fully meets passport photo requirements UK authorities enforce. No Photoshop. No photo booth queue. No software to install.

How to Create a Compliant UK Passport Photo — 3 Steps

  1. Upload Your Photo: Drag and drop any photo from your phone or camera. JPEG, PNG, and HEIC files are all accepted — no conversion needed. Maximum file size is 20 MB.
  2. Auto-Check & Fix: Our tool runs 30+ compliance checks against official UK passport photo standard rules — head position, eye line, background colour, lighting, and resolution — and corrects issues automatically.
  3. Download Print or Digital File: Get a print-ready 6×4 inch template with four passport photos, or a single digital file at the correct pixel dimensions for online renewal submissions. Both formats meet UK passport photo size requirements for HMPO and gov.uk applications.

Official UK Passport Photo Size and Specifications

The UK government publishes strict British passport photo guidelines that every application must meet. Below are the current official passport photo specifications UK applicants must follow for both printed and digital submissions.

Specification Printed Photo Digital Photo
Dimensions 35mm × 45mm (passport photo size UK cm: 3.5 × 4.5 cm) 600 × 750 pixels minimum
UK passport photo size in inches 1.37" × 1.77" N/A (pixel-based)
Aspect ratio 7:9 (passport photo ratio UK) 7:9
Resolution 600 DPI minimum UK passport photo size in pixels: min 600 × 750 px
Head height 29–34mm (chin to crown) 70–80% of frame height
Background Plain cream or white — UK passport size photo background colour Plain cream or white
File format (digital) N/A JPEG only, max 10 MB

Full British Passport Photo Checklist

Beyond dimensions, the photo requirements for British passport applications cover expression, clothing, and face visibility. Our tool checks all of the following automatically.

  • Face fully visible: No hair, hats, or scarves over your face. Religious head coverings are accepted but must not cast shadows.
  • Neutral expression: Mouth closed, eyes open, looking directly at the camera. No smiling.
  • No glasses: Passport photos ban all eyewear, including prescription glasses and sunglasses.
  • Plain background: Cream or light grey, with no shadows, patterns, or other people visible.
  • Even lighting: No shadows on the face or background.
  • Recent likeness: Taken within the last month.

UK Driving Licence Photo Requirements

DVLA driving licence photos follow the same 35 × 45mm biometric standard as passports, but two rules work differently — and both trip people up.

Can I wear glasses for my driving licence photo? Yes. Unlike a passport photo, DVLA rules let you keep your glasses on if you normally wear them. The only conditions: your eyes must be clearly visible, the frames must not cover them, and there must be no tint, glare, or reflection on the lenses. Sunglasses are never accepted. If the DVLA's automated scanner flags glare, the safest fix is to remove your glasses and retake the photo.

Driving licence photo size UK: 35mm wide × 45mm tall for a printed photo, or 600 × 750 pixels for a digital upload — identical to the passport spec, with the same 29–34mm head height and plain light-coloured background.

How many photos for a provisional driving licence? It depends on how you apply. Apply online via GOV.UK and you only need a digital photo upload — no printed copy required, and DVLA can often pull one from your passport record automatically. Apply by post using the D1 form and you need exactly one printed passport-style photo, signed on the back by a countersignatory if DVLA cannot verify your identity electronically. First provisional applications follow the same rules as renewals — there is no separate standard for new drivers.

What Are ICAO Biometric Photo Standards?

ICAO Document 9303 is the international standard behind almost every biometric ID photo, including UK passports, visas, and driving licences. It defines the technical rules that let facial recognition software read a photo reliably: head position and size within the frame, eye height, lighting uniformity, and image sharpness.

How to get an ICAO-compliant photo: face the camera directly with a neutral expression, keep both ears and the full face visible, use even lighting with no shadows or red-eye, and shoot against a plain, unpatterned light background. HMPO and UKVI then layer their own UK-specific rules — cream or light grey background, no glasses, and a maximum one-month photo age — on top of the base ICAO framework. Our built-in ICAO photo checker validates both layers in one pass, so a single upload satisfies the international standard and the UK-specific one together.

UK Visa Photo Requirements, Including Tourist Visas

UK tourist visa photo requirements match the standard 35 × 45mm biometric format used for Standard Visitor visas, Skilled Worker visas, Student visas, and family visas alike. For online applications through the UKVI portal or the UK ID Check app, you upload a digital JPEG of at least 600 × 750 pixels, sized between 50KB and 6MB, on a plain light-coloured background. If your visa route requires a biometric appointment or a postal submission, bring printed 35 × 45mm photos instead — check your specific appointment letter, since some visa centres request more than one print.

As with passports, glasses are not permitted in a UK visa photo, and the photo must be a true, unedited likeness with no digital retouching beyond background correction.

Digital vs Printed — UK Passport Photo Size Digital Explained

Since HMPO introduced the digital renewal pathway, many applicants now need a uk passport digital photo rather than a printed one. If you are renewing online via gov.uk, you will be asked to submit a digital photo or use the government's own UK passport online photo checker. Our tool generates both formats from a single upload — a digital JPEG at the correct UK passport photo size digital specification, and a printable 6×4 sheet for post applications or countersignature submissions.

The UK digital passport photo requirements differ slightly from printed ones: the file must be JPEG, at least 600 × 750 pixels, under 10 MB, and submitted through the official gov.uk portal or a recognised digital photo service. Our tool outputs a file that meets all of these criteria directly.

Frequently Asked Questions — UK Passport Photo Requirements

Do I need to wear glasses for a driver's licence photo?

No, wearing glasses is optional for a DVLA driving licence photo — it is your choice, not a requirement. If you do wear them, make sure your eyes are fully visible with no glare, shadow, or tint on the lenses. This is one of the few UK ID photos where glasses are allowed at all.

What is the standard UK passport photo size?

35mm wide × 45mm tall (3.5 × 4.5cm) for printed photos, or a minimum of 600 × 750 pixels for digital submissions, both at a 7:9 aspect ratio.

What is the driving licence photo size in the UK?

The same as a passport photo: 35 × 45mm printed, or 600 × 750 pixels digital, with a 29–34mm head height and a plain, light-coloured background.

How many photos do I need for a provisional driving licence?

None if you apply online — it's a digital upload only. By post with the D1 form, you need one printed photo, countersigned if DVLA cannot verify your identity another way.

How do I get an ICAO-compliant photo?

Use a plain light background, face forward with a neutral expression, keep your full face and both ears visible, and avoid shadows or glare. Our checker verifies your photo against ICAO Doc 9303 automatically before you download it.

What are the UK tourist visa photo requirements?

A 35 × 45mm biometric photo (or 600 × 750px digital upload), plain light background, neutral expression, and no glasses — the same standard used across most UK visa categories, including Standard Visitor visas.

What background colour does a UK passport photo need?

Plain cream or light grey, with no patterns, shadows, or objects behind you. Our tool replaces your background automatically to meet this rule.

Can I use this tool as an ICAO photo checker for other documents?

Yes. Beyond UK passports, visas, and driving licences, the same ICAO-based checks apply to most biometric ID photos worldwide — select your document type after upload for the matching size profile.

Can I use an online tool as a UK passport photo checker?

Yes. Our free UK passport photo checker validates your photo against all official HMPO biometric criteria before you submit. It checks dimensions, head position, background colour, lighting, and expression — and shows exactly which criteria pass or fail.

What are the UK passport renewal photo requirements?

The uk passport renewal photo requirements are identical to those for a new passport application — 35×45mm printed or 600×750px digital, plain cream or light grey background, neutral expression, no glasses, and taken within the last month. Our tool also supports passport photo renewal uk digital submissions via the gov.uk online system.

Does this tool work for UK visa photos too?

Yes — while this page focuses on passport photo requirements UK documents, the same tool also generates compliant photos for UK visa applications. Select your visa type after upload for the correct uk visa photo size and specification profile.

Is a UK passport photo template available to download?

Yes. After checking and correcting your image, you can download a ready-to-print UK passport photo template — a standard 6×4 inch sheet with four correctly sized and spaced photos, formatted for home printing or professional photo labs.

h1: Create ICAO Standard Photograph Online Free: Size, Specs & Checker
content:
What Is an ICAO Standard Photograph?

In short: an ICAO standard photograph is a passport-style portrait that follows the International Civil Aviation Organization biometric rules (Doc 9303): a plain light background, a neutral expression, open eyes, and a fixed head size, so border and e-gate systems can read your face. It is usually 35 × 45 mm (413 × 531 px at 300 DPI).

The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) sets the global biometric photo standard used by passport authorities, visa offices, and airport identity systems around the world. An ICAO standard photograph follows strict rules for head size, eye position, background color, lighting, and image sharpness so that facial recognition software can read it accurately at border control. Most countries base their national passport photo rules directly on ICAO standards, which is why a photo that meets ICAO specifications is accepted almost everywhere. Our tool builds a fully compliant ICAO standard photograph from any photo you upload, in under a minute, with no design software required.

How to Convert Your Photo to ICAO Standard — 3 Steps

You do not need to understand the technical specifications yourself. The tool applies them for you.

  1. Choose Your Document: Select the passport, visa, or ID type you need. The tool loads the exact ICAO-based profile for that document, including biometric ratios, background color, and resolution.
  2. Upload a Photo: Upload an existing photo or take a new one with your phone. JPEG, PNG, and WEBP files up to 15 MB work, from a camera roll, scanner, or gallery.
  3. Auto-Correct and Download: The tool removes the background, replaces it with the required color, aligns your face to the ICAO grid, and checks lighting and sharpness before you download the finished photo.

ICAO Photo Size and Specifications

These are the measurements an ICAO standard photo is built around. Exact print size and background shade vary by country, so always confirm with the authority that reviews your application.

RequirementICAO-based standard
Print size35 × 45 mm (most common). ICAO defines proportions, so some countries use another print size, for example 2 × 2 in in the US.
Digital size413 × 531 px at 300 DPI (35 × 45 mm)
Head height (chin to crown)About 70–80% of photo height, which is 32–36 mm on a 45 mm photo
Eye lineRoughly 50–60% of the way up from the bottom edge, with the head centred

Core Requirements of an ICAO Standard Photograph

ICAO photo standards exist to make sure a photo works both for a human officer at a counter and for automated facial recognition at an e-gate. The tool checks every one of these points automatically.

  • Head Position and Size: ICAO defines the exact proportion of the frame your head should occupy, measured from chin to crown. The tool uses facial landmark detection to align and crop your photo to this ratio precisely.
  • Neutral Background: A plain, evenly lit background — usually white or light grey — is a core ICAO requirement, since shadows or texture can confuse recognition software. The tool removes your original background and replaces it automatically.
  • Even, Shadow-Free Lighting: ICAO standards reject photos with shadows on the face or background. The tool detects lighting imbalance and corrects it so the final image is uniformly lit.
  • Neutral Expression, Open Eyes: A neutral expression with both eyes open and visible is required under ICAO guidelines. The tool flags photos with closed eyes, tilted heads, or exaggerated expressions so you can retake them if needed.
  • Resolution and Sharpness: ICAO sets a minimum resolution and sharpness threshold to keep facial features clearly readable. The tool outputs at the correct pixel dimensions and DPI for print or digital submission.

ICAO Standard Photograph vs Country-Specific Rules

Every member country of the International Civil Aviation Organization builds its national passport and visa photo rules on the same ICAO foundation, then adds small local variations. The United States, the United Kingdom, Schengen countries, India, and most others follow ICAO proportions for head size and expression, but differ slightly on background shade or final print size.

“2 Photos to ICAO Standards”: France and Schengen Forms

ICAO stands for the International Civil Aviation Organization, a United Nations agency that sets global standards for air travel, including the biometric photo specifications used in passports and travel documents. What is the ICAO photo size?

Some countries use a different print size, such as 2 × 2 in the US, but the head proportions follow the same ICAO logic. Pick your country in the tool and it applies the right size.

Is an ICAO standard photograph the same as a passport photo?

Not exactly, though the two overlap heavily. ICAO sets the international baseline for head position, background, lighting, and expression. Individual countries then add their own passport photo rules on top of that baseline, such as a specific print size or background shade.

Which documents require an ICAO standard photograph?

Passports, most visa applications, national ID cards, and airport biometric enrolment programs all rely on ICAO photo standards. The tool covers all of these document types by loading the correct profile once you select your destination.

Can I wear glasses, a hat or smile in an ICAO photo?

Glasses should be removed, or at minimum have no glare and show your eyes clearly. Hats and headphones are not allowed, except religious or medical head coverings that leave your full face visible. Keep a neutral expression with your mouth closed.

What does “2 photos to ICAO standards” mean on a French form?

French forms often ask for two identical, recent photos that meet ICAO biometric rules. In practice that means 35 × 45 mm, a plain light background, a neutral expression, and a correctly sized head. Create one compliant photo and print it twice.

Can I use an existing photo, or do I need a new one?

An existing photo often works well if your face is clear, well-lit, and facing forward. The tool corrects background, crop, and lighting automatically. If the original has closed eyes, heavy shadow, or extreme head tilt, a fresh photo will produce a more reliable result.

Will an ICAO standard photograph be accepted at every airport and embassy?

A photo built to ICAO standards is accepted by every country that bases its rules on the ICAO framework, which includes nearly all ICAO member states. Selecting your specific country in the tool applies any additional local rule on top of the ICAO baseline for full compliance.

  2. Upload or Click a Photo: Take a new photo with your phone or upload one from your gallery. JPEG, PNG, and HEIC files all work.
  3. Review and Download: The tool replaces the background, aligns your face, and flags any problems. Check the preview, then download your finished photo.

What You Need to Make Passport Photos at Home

You already own almost everything you need. Gather these items before you start.

Equipment

  • A smartphone or camera: Use the rear camera when possible. It gives a sharper image than the selfie camera.
  • A tripod or a helper: A steady camera at eye level keeps your face proportions accurate. A friend can also press the shutter.
  • A plain wall or sheet: A light, single-color surface gives the background removal a clean edge.

Space and Lighting

  • Stand about 1.5 metres from the camera.
  • Face a window so soft daylight lights your whole face.
  • Avoid direct sun, lamps behind you, and overhead lights that cast shadows under your eyes.

Passport Photo Requirements by Country

Every country builds its rules on the international ICAO biometric standard, then adds local details. The table below shows common examples. Always confirm the latest rules with the issuing authority.

Country Photo Size Background
United States2 x 2 in (51 x 51 mm)Plain white or off-white
United Kingdom35 x 45 mmPlain cream or light grey

Schengen Area35 x 45 mmLight, neutral color
Canada50 x 70 mmPlain white or light

You do not need to memorize these numbers. Select your country in the tool, and it applies the right profile for you.

Step-by-Step Guide to Click a Perfect Passport Photo

1. Set Up Your Background

Hang a plain sheet or stand in front of a bare wall. Keep at least one metre between you and the wall to reduce shadows.

2. Position the Camera

Place the camera at eye level and keep it straight. Shooting from above or below distorts your face and can cause a rejection.

3. Pose Correctly

Look straight at the lens. Keep your head upright, your mouth closed, and both eyes open. Relax your shoulders so they sit level.

4. Check the Result Before You Upload

Zoom in on the image. Look for blur, shadows across your face, red eyes, and stray hair over your eyes. Retake the photo if you spot any of these.

Common Passport Photo Mistakes and How to Fix Them

Mistake Why It Gets Rejected Quick Fix

Smiling or raised eyebrowsThe expression is not neutralRelax your face and close your mouth
Blurry imageFacial details are unreadableUse a tripod and clean the lens

Home Passport Photos vs Studio Photos

Tips to Pass Review on the First Attempt

  • Wear clothing that contrasts with your background. Avoid white shirts on a white wall.
  • Pull your hair back from your eyes and the outline of your face.
  • Remove hats, headphones, and heavy jewelry unless you wear a religious head covering. Your face must stay fully visible.
  • Take several shots and pick the sharpest one.
  • Check whether your application needs a printed photo or a digital file, then select the matching output.

Official Government References

Verify current photo specifications directly with official portals:

  • ICAO – International Civil Aviation Organization (Official Site)
  • GOV.UK – Official UK Passport Photo Guidelines

Frequently Asked Questions About Taking Passport Photos at Home

Can I take my own passport photo with a phone?

Yes. Most authorities accept self-taken photos if they meet the rules for size, background, and quality. Use good light, keep the camera at eye level, and let the tool fix the background and crop.

Are free passport photos at home really accepted?

Authorities judge the photo, not where you made it. A photo that meets the official specifications is accepted whether you took it at home or in a studio. Our tool lets you preview the result for free before you download.

What background should I use at home?

Use a plain, light wall or sheet. The tool then replaces it with the exact color your country requires, so you do not need a perfect backdrop.

Can I print the photo myself?

Yes, if your application accepts printed photos. Print on high-quality photo paper at the correct size. Many services also print for you, and some applications only need a digital upload.

Can I wear glasses in my passport photo?

Most countries ask you to remove glasses because of glare and shadows. Check your country's rules, and take them off if you are unsure.

Does the tool work on a phone?

Yes. It runs in your mobile browser, so you can take the photo, edit it, and download it from one device without installing an app.

How much does it cost?

Uploading, editing, and previewing are free. A small fee applies only when you download the final high-resolution, watermark-free file.

title: Take Passport Photo With iPhone – US, UK, CA & AU Guide
metaDescription: Take a passport photo with your iPhone the right way. Check US, UK, Canada and Australia rules, then create a compliant photo online.
h1: How to Take a Passport Photo With iPhone: US, UK, Canada & Australia
content:
You can take a passport photo with an iPhone and use it for a US, UK or Australian application. Your camera is sharp enough, so the real work is setup: plain background, even light and a straight-on pose. Our tool then crops the photo, replaces the background and checks your head size before you download.

One important exception applies. Canada requires a commercial photographer for passport photos, so an iPhone photo does not work there. This guide covers the rules for all four countries, so you know what to expect before you start.

Can You Take a Passport Photo With an iPhone?

Most passport authorities judge the final photo, not the device. If the size, background, lighting and expression meet the rules, an iPhone photo passes. Here is how the four countries compare.

Where iPhone Passport Photos Are Accepted

CountryCan you use an iPhone photo?What to know
United StatesYesUpload a digital photo online or print a 2 x 2 in photo. Make sure the file meets the digital rules.
United KingdomYesUpload a digital photo to the gov.uk service, or print 35 x 45 mm photos for a paper form.
AustraliaYesYou can take your own photo if it meets the rules. Paper applications need printed photos, and some need a guarantor signature.
CanadaNo, for passportsCanada requires a commercial photographer, and the photographer must add details to the photo. An iPhone photo will not qualify.

Always confirm the current rules on the official website before you apply. Guidance changes, and different application routes can have different requirements.

Passport Photo Requirements for the US, UK, Canada and Australia

Every country builds its rules on the international ICAO biometric standard, then adds local details. This table shows the main specifications side by side.

CountryPhoto sizeHead height (chin to crown)BackgroundDigital filePhoto age
United States2 x 2 in (51 x 51 mm)1 to 1⅜ in (25–35 mm)Plain white or off-whiteSquare JPEG, 600 x 600 to 1200 x 1200 px, up to 240 KBWithin 6 months
United Kingdom35 x 45 mm29–34 mmPlain cream or light greyJPEG, at least 600 x 750 px, 50 KB to 10 MBRecent, ideally within the last month
Canada50 x 70 mm31–36 mmPlain white or lightCommercial photographer supplies itWithin 6 months
Australia35 x 45 mm (35–40 x 45–50 mm accepted)32–36 mmPlain light colourCheck the current application routeWithin 6 months

Expression, Glasses and Headwear

These rules are similar across all four countries:

  • Expression: Keep a neutral expression with both eyes open and your mouth closed. The US also allows a natural, subtle smile.
  • Glasses: Take them off. Exceptions apply only for documented medical reasons, and even then you must avoid glare and tint.
  • Headwear: Hats and caps are not allowed. Religious head coverings are fine if your full face stays visible from chin to forehead.
  • Editing: Do not use filters, retouching or beauty modes.

How to Take a Passport Photo With iPhone in 3 Steps

  1. Take the photo. Use the rear camera against a plain wall in soft daylight, following the steps below.
  2. Upload it. Choose your country and document in the tool, then upload the picture. It accepts JPEG, PNG and HEIC files.
  3. Review and download. The tool crops the image, replaces the background and flags problems. Check the preview, then download your file. The same steps work for visas and other ID photos.

How to Take a Passport Photo From iPhone: Step by Step

Set Up Your Space

  • Face a window so daylight falls evenly on your face.
  • Avoid direct sun, lamps behind you and overhead lights that cast shadows.
  • Stand in front of a plain, light wall, and keep frames and furniture out of the shot.
  • Stand about one metre from the wall to reduce shadows behind your head.
  • Wear a top that contrasts with the wall.

Change Your iPhone Camera Settings

  • Camera: Use the rear camera, not the selfie camera.
  • Mode: Choose Photo, not Portrait. Portrait mode blurs and alters the edges of your head.
  • Flash and Live Photo: Turn both off.
  • Filters: Set the filter to Original. If your iPhone has Photographic Styles, choose Standard.
  • Grid: Turn on Grid in Settings > Camera to help you centre your head.
  • Format: If you upload directly to an official portal, choose Most Compatible in Settings > Camera > Formats. This saves JPEG files instead of HEIC.

Position Your iPhone and Pose

  • Hold the phone at eye level. A camera that points up or down distorts your face.
  • Stand about 1 to 1.5 metres away, and leave space around your head for cropping.
  • Look straight at the lens with your head level and shoulders square.
  • Use the timer if you shoot alone, or ask a helper to press a volume button.
  • Take several shots and choose the sharpest one.

Check Your Photo Before You Upload

Open the picture in the Photos app and zoom in. Look for blur, shadows, hair over your eyes and a tilted head. Retake the photo if you spot any of these.

How to Take a 2x2 Passport Photo on iPhone

The US uses a square 2 x 2 inch photo. You can shoot it the same way, then square it up on your iPhone.

  1. Open the photo in Photos and tap Edit.
  2. Tap the Crop icon and choose Square.
  3. Keep your head in the middle, with space above it.
  4. Upload the result to our tool and select the US passport or visa option.

The tool then sets the head height, background and file size. US digital photos must be square JPEG files between 600 x 600 and 1200 x 1200 pixels and no larger than 240 KB.

Using Your iPhone Photo for the UK, Canada or Australia

United Kingdom

The gov.uk service accepts a digital photo you take yourself. Your head must measure 29–34 mm from chin to crown on a plain cream or light grey background. Paper applications need printed 35 x 45 mm photos, and some need a countersignature on the back.

Canada

Canada is different. Passport photos must be taken by a commercial photographer, and the photographer must add the studio name, address and date on the back of one print. This rule applies to the photo itself, so no home photo or app can replace it. Some other Canadian immigration applications have different photo rules, so read the instructions for your specific form.

Australia

Australia asks for a 35 x 45 mm photo with a head height of 32–36 mm on a plain light background. You can take your own photo if it meets these rules. Paper applications may need a guarantor to sign the back of one photo, so check the current requirements for your application type.

Do You Need a Passport Photo App on iPhone?

No. Our tool works in Safari, so you can go from camera roll to finished file without installing anything. Select your country and document, upload your photo and preview the result for free. You pay only if you download the final file.

How to Print Your iPhone Passport Photo

Printed photos are needed for many paper applications. You have two easy options:

  1. Print at a shop or kiosk. Save the print sheet to your iPhone, take it to a pharmacy or photo kiosk, and ask for a 6 x 4 inch print with no cropping.
  2. Print at home with AirPrint. Tap Share, tap Print and choose your printer. Load glossy or matt photo paper and select the highest quality.

Print at 100% scale, then measure one photo with a ruler to confirm the size. Plain office paper is not suitable.

Common iPhone Passport Photo Mistakes and How to Fix Them

MistakeWhy it gets rejectedFix
Selfie distortionThe lens stretches your nose and foreheadUse the rear camera from about 1 to 1.5 metres
Shadows on the wallUneven light hides your featuresFace a window and stand away from the wall
Beauty filtersThe photo no longer looks like youUse the Original filter and skip edits
Glasses or glareReflections hide your eyesTake glasses off unless you have a medical reason
Wrong print scalePrinters shrink photos to fit the pagePrint at 100% scale and measure with a ruler

Official Government References

  • U.S. Department of State – Passport Photo Requirements
  • GOV.UK – Official UK Passport Photo Guidelines
  • Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)
  • Australian Passport Office

Frequently Asked Questions About iPhone Passport Photos

Can I take a passport photo with my iPhone?

Yes, for the US, UK and Australia. Authorities judge the final photo, not the camera. Your iPhone photo must meet the size, background, lighting and expression rules. Canada is the exception for passports.

Can I take a Canadian passport photo on my iPhone?

No. Canadian passport photos must come from a commercial photographer, who also adds details to the back of one print. You can still practise the pose or use an iPhone photo for other documents that allow self-taken photos, but check the exact rules first.

How do I take a passport photo with an iPhone by myself?

Rest your iPhone on a stand or a stack of books at eye level, about 1 to 1.5 metres away. Turn on the timer in the Camera app, step into position and take several shots. A helper gives better results, but the timer works well.

Do I need a passport photo app on iPhone?

No. Our tool runs in Safari, so you do not need to install anything. You can upload JPEG, PNG or HEIC files straight from your camera roll.

Requirements can change. Always confirm the current specifications with the issuing authority before you submit your application. We are an independent service, not affiliated with any government.
